macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: RBA holds cash rate at 4.35% and warns inflation remains elevated
items.summary: Australia’s central bank left its policy rate unchanged at 4.35% and said inflation is still elevated, while signaling it could hike again if needed. The decision was unanimous.

items.title: Singapore Q2 GDP growth beats expectations, lifting 2026 forecast
items.summary: Singapore reported 5.9% year-over-year GDP growth in Q2, above expectations, and the government raised its 2026 growth forecast on stronger AI-driven demand. The economy expanded 1.4% quarter over quarter.

items.title: Wall Street closes lower as Hormuz deal hopes fade
items.summary: The Nasdaq and S&P 500 ended lower on Monday as investors grew less confident that a deal would reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Reuters cited declines in Intel and other chipmakers as part of the move.

items.title: US markets show mixed overnight moves, with Asian stocks firmer
items.summary: Reuters’ market snapshot showed the S&P 500 down 0.06%, the Euro STOXX 50 up 0.18%, the FTSE 100 down 0.35%, and the Nikkei 225 up 2.08%. The same snapshot showed the US 10-year yield at 4.705%.

items.title: Nvidia partners with major banks to raise over $500 billion for AI infrastructure
items.summary: Nvidia said it is working with six major financial institutions to launch compute financing platforms aimed at raising more than $500 billion in third-party capital for AI buildout. The announcement underscores continued AI-related capital spending.

items.title: Intel plans a $15 billion share sale amid turnaround rally
items.summary: Reuters reported that Intel plans a $15 billion share sale as part of its turnaround efforts. The news came alongside a broader move in chip stocks tied to changing market sentiment.

items.title: SEC settles charges over SpaceX, Klarna and pre-IPO share fraud
items.summary: Reuters reported that the SEC settled charges involving SpaceX, Klarna, and a pre-IPO share fraud case. The action highlights continued regulatory scrutiny in private-market investing.

items.title: US SEC eases rules for data center bonds
items.summary: The SEC said it will make it easier for data center owners to sell asset-backed securities by exempting certain data center bonds from key securitization rules. The move could support AI infrastructure financing.

items.title: Hims & Hers reports wider quarterly loss on obesity-drug strategy
items.summary: Reuters reported that Hims & Hers posted a wider quarterly loss after shifting toward branded obesity drugs. The result was one of several notable company developments cited in the latest market flow.

items.title: GM plans to sell its half of Indiana battery venture to Samsung SDI
items.summary: Reuters reported that GM intends to sell its stake in its Indiana battery joint venture to Samsung SDI. The move is another sign of reshaping EV and battery partnerships.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin holds around $65K as market sentiment improves
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $65,000 and ether hovered near $1,925 as crypto markets opened the week in the green, with risk assets stabilizing after recent turbulence. Monero led gains among major coins, briefly topping $400, while NEAR and FET also recovered.

items.title: Bitcoin, Ethereum and XRP dip as liquidation pressure hits crypto market
items.summary: Major cryptocurrencies fell on Monday, with bitcoin near $63,977, ether around $1,874, and XRP near $1.01 as broader risk appetite weakened. More than $200 million was liquidated in the crypto market over 24 hours, mostly from long positions.

items.title: Grayscale withdraws Cardano, Hedera and Polkadot ETF filings
items.summary: Grayscale reportedly pulled its ETF filings tied to Cardano, Hedera, and Polkadot, a notable setback for altcoin ETF ambitions. The move adds fresh uncertainty to the regulatory path for these products.

items.title: Europe moves toward a MiCA rewrite to curb foreign stablecoins
items.summary: European policymakers are preparing to revise MiCA rules to rein in foreign stablecoins by 2027. The proposal signals continued regulatory tightening around cross-border digital-asset issuance and use.

items.title: Upbit to list DOS token on KRW, BTC and USDT markets
items.summary: South Korean exchange Upbit announced it will list DOS, with trading set to begin at 14:00 local time on August 11. The listing expands access to the token across fiat and major crypto markets.

items.title: RWA DeFi total value locked reaches $3.9 billion
items.summary: Real-world asset DeFi activity continued to grow, with total value locked reaching $3.9 billion. Crypto.com also highlighted Dubai Duty Free integrating Crypto.com Pay, pointing to ongoing payments adoption.

items.title: Samsung Wallet reportedly adding stablecoin accounts and cross-border payments
items.summary: A report said Samsung Wallet will add stablecoin accounts and cross-border payment features this year. If implemented, the move would be a notable consumer-payments step for crypto integration.

items.title: Strategy converts 1,690 BTC into a $108.6M STRC buyback
items.summary: Cointelegraph reported that Strategy used 1,690 bitcoin to support a $108.6 million STRC buyback. The transaction highlights continued corporate treasury activity involving bitcoin holdings.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Meta launches new open-weight AI model and signals more releases soon
items.summary: Meta released **Muse Glimmer**, an open-weight model, and signaled plans to launch an open-weight version of its most advanced model in the coming weeks. The move underscores Meta’s continued push toward open model distribution and distillation-based training.

items.title: OpenAI expands its Daybreak cybersecurity program with new model tiers
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled **Daybreak Blue** for frontier model access and **Daybreak Red** for purpose-trained cybersecurity models, while also expanding its Daybreak defense program. The company is positioning the release around safer, more controlled use for cyber defenders.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-5.6-Cyber to selected partners
items.summary: OpenAI introduced **GPT-5.6-Cyber**, described as a more cyber-permissive version of GPT-5.6 Sol, for vetted partners. The release appears aimed at autonomous cyber defense and controlled offensive-security testing.

items.title: Anthropic makes Claude Sonnet 5 pricing permanent
items.summary: Anthropic said the introductory pricing for **Claude Sonnet 5** will remain at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, canceling a planned September 1 increase. The decision suggests competitive pressure in model pricing remains intense.

items.title: Anthropic adopts EU AI Act compliance measures for Claude outputs
items.summary: Anthropic said Claude models in the EU will add **invisible watermarks** to generated text and **C2PA metadata** to generated files to comply with the EU AI Act. This is part of a broader industry trend toward provenance and content authentication.

items.title: Nvidia reportedly backs a $500 billion AI infrastructure funding package
items.summary: Nvidia is reported to be partnering with major financial firms including Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR on a **$500 billion** funding package for AI infrastructure. The deal highlights the scale of capital flowing into data centers and compute buildout.

items.title: Anthropic signs major compute deal with Riot Platforms
items.summary: Reports say Anthropic agreed to a **20-year, $9.1 billion** compute deal with Riot Platforms for 191 MW of capacity at a Texas campus. The agreement reflects continued scarcity of large-scale AI compute infrastructure.

items.title: Singapore raises growth forecast on AI investment boom
items.summary: Singapore raised its 2026 growth forecast, citing stronger-than-expected **global AI investment** as a key support for activity. The report is another sign that AI spending is influencing macroeconomic forecasts beyond the tech sector.

items.title: OpenAI pauses some model work over cybersecurity concerns
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that OpenAI paused some work on a new AI model because of **cybersecurity concerns**. The move shows safety review is still affecting model development timelines.

items.title: AI infrastructure spending continues to drive industry trends
items.summary: Recent reporting points to accelerating investment in **data centers, compute capacity, and AI infrastructure**, with companies and investors treating AI demand as a major growth engine. This includes large capital commitments and new facility development across the sector.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Epic Games to sell ArtStation and Sketchfab to Kitbash
items.summary: Epic Games is offloading ArtStation and Sketchfab, two creator-focused platforms it acquired in 2021. Kitbash, a 3D assets company for games, will take over the properties.

items.title: Steam hardware shipper breach may have exposed customer data
items.summary: Valve says customer data was “likely compromised” in a breach tied to a Steam hardware shipper. Reported exposed information includes names and addresses.

items.title: Xbox and PC gamers in Australia may soon face age verification for 18+ games
items.summary: Microsoft is reportedly notifying adult Xbox and PC users in Australia that they will need to verify their age before buying 18+ rated apps and games. The rollout is expected to begin later in August 2026.

items.title: Minecraft coming to Switch 2 in October
items.summary: Minecraft is set to launch on Nintendo Switch 2 on October 27, expanding the game’s platform availability with a next-gen release.

items.title: Nintendo to release Star Fox 64 remake as a Switch 2 exclusive
items.summary: Nintendo is reportedly bringing a remake of Star Fox 64 to Switch 2 as an exclusive release. The game is said to arrive on June 25.

items.title: GTA VI preorders reportedly off to an exceptional start
items.summary: Preorders for Grand Theft Auto VI are reportedly performing exceptionally well. The report suggests unusually strong early demand ahead of release.

items.title: Quake gets a new free expansion
items.summary: A new free expansion has been released for Quake, giving longtime fans fresh content for the classic shooter. The update is notable as another revival of a legacy id Software title.

items.title: Big Walk hits 1 million copies in six days
items.summary: House House and Panic say Big Walk sold over a million copies across all platforms in less than a week. The milestone is notable for far outpacing the sales pace of Untitled Goose Game.

items.title: Hellraiser: Revival gameplay shown, Steam page confirmed
items.summary: IGN shared 14 minutes of gameplay for Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival and the footage confirmed the game already has a Steam page. Saber Interactive says the horror game is scheduled for October 8, 2026.

items.title: Overwatch season overhaul announced
items.summary: Blizzard is changing Overwatch’s progression system in the upcoming Heroes of Busan update. The new structure replaces the linear battle pass with five shorter paths and adds limited-time return passes.

items.title: Microsoft to require age verification for adult Xbox users in Australia
items.summary: Microsoft announced that adult Xbox accounts in Australia will soon need to confirm their age before accessing 18+ apps and games. The requirement will apply to both console and PC storefronts.

items.title: Aliens: Fireteam Elite cloud version on Switch is no longer playable
items.summary: Owners of the Switch cloud version of Aliens: Fireteam Elite can no longer access the game after the required cloud service was shut down. The title is now permanently unavailable to those buyers.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Nvidia partners with Wall Street giants on a $500 billion funding push for data center expansion
items.summary: Nvidia is working with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR on a financing package aimed at accelerating AI infrastructure buildout. Reuters says the effort would raise more than $500 billion in third-party capital for compute financing platforms.

items.title: Intel plans a $15 billion share sale as its turnaround rally continues
items.summary: Reuters reports Intel is preparing a large share sale while its stock has recently risen on optimism around the company’s turnaround efforts. The move underscores how chipmakers remain central to broader market and supply-chain developments.

items.title: Google Play adds Venmo as a payment option in the U.S.
items.summary: Google is expanding payment choices on Google Play by adding Venmo for games, apps, add-ons, and subscriptions. The change widens support beyond PayPal and Cash App for U.S. users.

items.title: U.S. SEC eases securitization rules for certain data center bonds
items.summary: Reuters says the SEC has exempted certain data center bonds from key securitization rules, making it easier for owners to sell asset-backed securities. The decision reflects how data center financing is becoming more important as cloud and infrastructure demand grows.

items.title: OpenAI expands its cybersecurity initiative with a more cyber-permissive model
items.summary: Techmeme reports OpenAI has released GPT-5.6-Cyber to some partners and expanded its Daybreak cybersecurity program. The company is positioning the model for vetted defenders as it prepares for more autonomous cyber threats.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly completes a $7 billion employee tender offer
items.summary: TechCrunch reports OpenAI has completed a large employee tender offer, giving staff a chance to sell shares. The deal is one of the biggest company-financing developments reported in the past day.
